feature: The Secondary button frosts what is behind it
summary: A Secondary Button dropped over a screenshot now softens what is behind it, like the mock's glass, so busy detail no longer shows through sharp behind its words. Any shape can do the same: add a Blur and set its Kind to Background.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/secondary-button-glass-walk.json.

try.do: Open a busy screenshot (code, a web page, anything with small text).
Drag the Button from the Library's Comps onto the busiest part and pick Secondary in Variant.
Zoom in on the button: the text under it should be a soft wash, the text around it sharp.
Try it over the dark artboard too: the glass picks up the colour behind it.
Draw a rectangle, set its Opacity to 20, press the plus on Effects and choose Blur.
Click Background on the Blur row's Kind: the rectangle goes crisp and what is under it goes soft.
Export the picture as PNG and compare it with the canvas.

evaluate: Does the Secondary button over a busy screenshot read as glass rather than a pale sticker?
Are the button's words easy to read over the busiest part of your screenshots?
Is Kind with Layer and Background on the Blur row where you would look for frosted glass, or would you expect a separate Background Blur in the plus menu, as Figma has?
Is 12 points of softness right for a button, or should it be softer or sharper?
rough: Matches the variants mock's glass (ui-variants.html, the Secondary cells; button.css .btn and --lg-blur-sm): white at 74% over the backdrop, blurred by 12 with saturation at 180%.
The layer's Opacity fades its paint, not the glass, so a fade-in on a frosted layer shows the blur at full strength from the first frame. Lower the blur's Amount to fade the glass.
A copy of the Button placed before this change keeps the Button it was saved with, so it has no glass until it is swapped or the Button is dropped again.
SVG export has no way to say 'blur what is behind', so an exported SVG shows the 74% white without the glass. PNG and every other picture export match the canvas.
